title: Define animation-ready pose contract and reusable indexed pose buffer
description:
## Summary
The current rig can apply an indexed `PosedSkeleton`, but that payload stores only absolute positions and reconstructs rotations from child directions. That is sufficient for the current procedural/IK proof and insufficient for general animation because terminal twist, explicit local rotation, and rotation without endpoint movement are not representable. Define one animation-ready indexed pose contract and a reusable buffer without introducing an Animator/state-machine framework.

## Scope
- Define an indexed pose payload with explicit position and rotation semantics. Prefer local/parent-relative bone transforms if the actor-root contract is adopted; otherwise explicitly document the current absolute creature-space bridge and the conversion boundary.
- Define whether local position is animated, rest position is fixed, and whether scale is unsupported or explicitly represented.
- Define rotation normalization, finite-value requirements, terminal-bone behavior, root/pelvis semantics, mirror behavior, and compatibility with `SkeletonSnapshot` ordering/signature.
- Provide a caller-owned reusable `PoseBuffer` or equivalent indexed storage so steady-state animation does not clone arrays or allocate dictionaries.
- Keep `PosedSkeleton` as a useful immutable/debug/procedural snapshot only if its compatibility role remains justified; do not make it the required per-frame construction path.
- Preserve `PoseRotationResolver` as a procedural/IK conversion utility, not as the definition of animation pose.
- Define the adapter from explicit animation pose data into the existing `CreatureRig` and `LinearBlendSkinning` conventions.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A terminal bone can rotate/twist while its endpoint position remains unchanged.
- An interior bone can receive an explicit rotation without deriving it from a child direction.
- The same indexed pose order is consumed by `CreatureRig`, SMR binding, and the pure LBS oracle.
- Reusing a pose buffer across repeated samples produces zero managed allocations after warmup; no per-frame dictionary or whole-pose clone is required.
- Pose buffers reject non-finite position/rotation input at the boundary.
- Local/absolute transform semantics, root-motion ownership, scale policy, mirror rule, and compatibility identity are documented and tested.
- Existing IK position-based tests remain valid by converting IK output into the explicit pose representation.

## Validation
- Runtime unit tests for terminal twist, interior explicit rotation, finite validation, buffer reuse, and skeleton compatibility.
- PlayMode test on a real generated creature proving an explicit terminal rotation deforms the SMR without requiring endpoint movement.
- Repeated end-to-end pose production plus `CreatureRig.ApplyPose` allocation measurement after warmup.
- No Animator, Avatar, gait, locomotion, or clip-controller implementation in this task.

## Findings
This task is a new representation-level boundary, not a reopening of the fixed continuation-child rotation defect. The prior fix makes procedural position poses better, but animation still cannot express arbitrary rotations. `PosedSkeleton` currently stores only positions, while `PoseRotationResolver` derives rotations and keeps terminal bones at rest rotation. The current external-driver ADR correctly selects direct indexed pose application; this task strengthens the payload that crosses that boundary.

## Blockers
The actor-local versus absolute pose decision must be made before a final API is frozen. Coordinate with TSK-0073 and TSK-0203; do not add a second competing transform convention.

## Next Step
Write the pose-space decision record, define the indexed buffer shape, then add focused math/runtime tests before connecting any real animation source.

comments.body: Created from the 2026-09-09 cross-audit synthesis. The current indexed CreatureRig hot path is healthy, but `PosedSkeleton` remains position-only and `WithUpdatedPositions` clones its full array. This task captures the missing animation representation without introducing an internal Animator framework. Provenance: animation/deformation follow-up audit, TSK-0073, ADR-010, current PosedSkeleton/PoseRotationResolver source.
